long_biography.plain_text:
Charles Butt entered H-E-B at eight, bagging groceries in the company his grandmother Florence founded. He succeeded his father as president in 1971, inheriting a regional chain with roughly 120 stores and $221 million in annual sales. Over the next five decades, he made store-level adaptation, private-label products and new formats central to the retailer's expansion, while extending the business into Mexico. Revenue rose into the tens of billions before he handed the chief executive role to his nephew Howard Butt III in 2021.

Butt remained chairman of the family-controlled company and broadened employee ownership through a stock plan granting shares to eligible staff. Education became his main philanthropic focus. He founded The Holdsworth Center to develop public-school leaders, drawing inspiration from his mother, Mary Elizabeth Holdsworth, a former teacher. His record combines inherited ownership with sustained personal operation: he received a mature family business, then transformed its scale, formats and institutions.
